record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist a theory with more supersymmetry than N = 8 supergravity, possibly an N = 16 theory with a twelve-dimensional origin, for which the Reissner–Nordström black-hole embeddings that are non-supersymmetric inside N = 8 become supersymmetric while N = 8 remains a consistent truncation?

evidence.quote: The non-supersymmetric embeddings (that is, supersymmetric embeddings without unbroken SUSY) share many properties with the supersymmetric ones (after all, they have the same metric): Bogomol'nyi-like identities are satisfied [10] and the solutions seem to have the same stability properties [11].

This may suggest that there is a theory with more SUSY (N = 16?), of which N = 8 is a consistent truncation, in which all of these embeddings are supersymmetric [12, 10]. This theory may have a 12-dimensional origin.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider four-dimensional N=8 supergravity and the standard embeddings of the Reissner–Nordström black-hole solution into this theory. Some of these embeddings preserve a fraction of the N=8 supersymmetry, while others, although sharing the same metric and satisfying Bogomol'nyi-type identities and analogous stability properties, do not preserve any of the N=8 supersymmetries (the so-called non-supersymmetric extreme embeddings).

Question: Does there exist a supergravity theory with strictly more supersymmetry than N=8 (for instance an N=16 theory, possibly with a twelve-dimensional origin) such that
(i) N=8 supergravity arises as a consistent truncation of this larger theory, and
(ii) every Reissner–Nordström embedding that fails to be supersymmetric within N=8 supergravity is supersymmetric when lifted to this larger theory (i.e., preserves some of its additional supersymmetries)?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface known N=16 gauged supergravities in three dimensions and consistent truncations of 10/11-dimensional supergravity, but no source confirms a four-dimensional theory with more supersymmetry than N=8 (with a possible twelve-dimensional origin) that admits N=8 as a consistent truncation and renders the non-supersymmetric Reissner–Nordström embeddings supersymmetric. The status of the proposal therefore appears unresolved/speculative in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: N=8 supergravity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: N=8 supergravity is the most symmetric quantum field theory which involves gravity and a finite number of fields in four spacetime dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: N=8 in four dimensions is the maximal known supergravity, with no established 4d parent of higher supersymmetry.

status_evidence.title: Consistent Truncations and Generalised Geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Consistent truncations preserving various amounts of supersymmetry can be defined in terms of generalised G-structures in Exceptional Field Theory.
status_evidence.claim: Modern consistent-truncation framework does not list a 12d/N=16 parent of 4d N=8 of the form proposed.
